topic: Packing the car for a holiday road trip

slides.headline: Packing the car for a road trip?
slides.sub: A few loading habits that make the first leg easier on your back.

slides.title: Heavy bags in first
slides.body: Load the heaviest bags first, close to the back seats, so you're not reaching over them later. Bend your knees, bring each bag close and slide it in rather than swinging it.

slides.title: Don't lean deep into the boot
slides.body: Leaning far into the boot with a heavy bag at arm's length is a classic back tweak. Step in close, rest the bag on the bumper edge first, then slide it into place.

slides.title: Smaller bags, more trips
slides.body: One enormous bag is tempting but awkward to lift. Several medium bags are easier to handle and pack more neatly. An extra walk to the car is a small price.

slides.title: Set your seat before you go
slides.body: Sit close enough to reach the pedals with a slight bend in your knees, with your back supported by the seat. Set your mirrors once you're sitting well, so you don't slump later.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Back pain after packing that spreads down a leg, comes with numbness or weakness, or isn't easing after a few days is worth getting assessed.

slides.headline: Back sore after holiday packing?
slides.body: Our chiropractors look at how you lift and move, and pair hands-on care with simple exercises. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
The road trip starts in the driveway, and so do a lot of holiday back tweaks. 🚗

Packing the car means lots of lifting at awkward angles, often in a rush. Leaning deep into the boot with a heavy bag at arm's length is one of the most common culprits.

Load the heavy bags first and close to the seats, rest bags on the bumper edge before sliding them in, and choose a few medium bags over one giant one. Set up your seat and mirrors properly before you leave, and plan regular stops to get out and move.
